recipes.name: Mother-In-Law Eggs
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon spicy brown mustard (such as Gulden's®)
1 teaspoon hot mustard (such as Sweet Hot Mister Mustard®)
6 pimento-stuffed green olives, cut in half

steps.text: Place eggs into a medium saucepan in a single layer and fill with water to cover eggs by 1 inch. Cover the saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Remove from heat and let eggs stand in hot water for 15 minutes. Drain. Cool eggs under cold running water, then peel and halve eggs lengthwise. Scoop yolks into a large bowl; mash yolks with a fork.
Stir mayonnaise, spicy brown mustard, hot mustard, sugar, salt, and pepper into mashed yolks until well combined. Spoon into a quart-size, resealable plastic bag. Snip a corner off the plastic bag.
Squeeze yolk mixture into egg white halves. Sprinkle each stuffed egg with paprika and top with an olive half.

raw_recipe.headline: Mother-In-Law Eggs
raw_recipe.description: Deviled eggs made with spicy hot mustard have a sweet and hot kick. A cut stuffed olive on top adds to the presentation.

review.reviewBody: Save an extra clean-up step by putting all the ingredients to be mixed into the zip type bag, "massage" it all together and then snip a corner off & squeeze it into the egg halves.

This is a great recipe! I really enjoyed these eggs. Since my family isn't into spicy, I used regular yellow and dijon mustard instead of the spicy and hot mustards. I also skipped the pimento stuffed olives...I didn't have any, and my family doesn't care for them. I found that the best way to make a nice, smooth filling that's easy to pipe is to use my hand mixer to mash the yolks, and then beat in the other ingredients. I made one recipe the first time, and they were so good that Geranium and I just made a double batch. Thanks for sharing the recipe...these are great!!!!!

This recipe is closest to our family recipe. I have tried many other deviled egg recipes on this site but my family likes the traditional plain eggs. I use 1/4 c. mayonnaise instead of 2 tbsp. as we like it creamier. I do not use hot mustard in this as family does not like it. I used a pastry blender to break up the yolk which made it very smooth. When you pipe the filling in, it looks so pretty and the addition of the sliced olive on top always brings an "Oh, these are so gorgeous". If you don't have an egg plate, I lay these on a bed of shredded lettuce which makes it pretty. Make lots as they go fast.

I boiled the eggs the day before, then mixed everything in the food processor. Turned out creamy and delish! Topped with chives instead of olives. I actually doubled the recipe because I have some serious deviled egg eaters in this family! This was the first thing to go they all loved them! This is a keeper in our house! Thanks for the recipe Shorecook!

unbelievably delicious! instead of hot mustard I added a little pickle relish. in the end I added another 1/2 tablespoon of mayo too. I also mixed the egg yolk filling with a hand mixer. It made it very fluffy. Love it!

I used Hot & Sweet Mustard from another site (none on AR yet) for the one teaspoon called for here. I use extra large eggs, so the mixture was too dry to pipe until I added a second teaspoon of the hot sweet mustard. With extra large yolks, next time I'll add an extra teaspoon of mayo to make it a bit creamier. It is a nice change from the standard deviled eggs. I'm sure the original amounts are fine with regular large eggs.
I’ve made this recipe all my life, only difference is we called it Mothe-in-Law Eyes. I use both green and black olives to alternate colors. They are a favorite in my family.
Excellent deviled egg recipe! Although, I substituted Nance's Original Sharp & Creamy Mustard. That is my all time favorite mustard to use in deviled eggs, potato salad, etc.

These are our favorite deviled eggs now but with a few changes. My kids are not too keen about spicy mustard so I cut the spicy brown mustard in half. And I don't ever have hot mustard on hand so I use regular mustard with a few shots of Tabasco. Then I also add about a teaspoon of pickle relish, the tanginess works well with the other flavors.

Fantastic recipe for deviled eggs! This is the recipe my mom taught me to make except she uses yellow mustard and no sugar. I thought the spicy and hot mustard gave this a nice twist, and the green olive on top was a great addition.

Awesome, shorecook! I made this recipe exact, only leaving off the olives only because we don't like them. I made these early this morning to use up the remaining eggs before shopping day. It's got this whole sweet-hot thing going on. I can't have sugar and eggs are low-carb so next batch, I might leave out the sugar next time but that's a personal choice, not reflective of the recipe. I'm beginning to rethink deviled eggs....the last two recipes I made were AWESOME! NOTE: I couldn't find my cool tips to make pretty filled eggs, so I just scooped the filling into a thick freezer bag and snipped off the edge. Wa-la, instant piping bag.
One of my family’s favorites. I like that you can adjust how hot you want it. Great recipe.
Loved it! Will absolutely make it again and again. I loved the change in flavor from the traditional deviled eggs. Only one complaint from grandson - he didn't like the olive on top LOL.
This a great twist on deviled eggs.
Very good, followed directions and they were perfect

I was in agreement with a few other reviewers, didn't care for the pimento olives and prefer regular and Dijon mustard so by the time those changes are made, it isn't the same recipe. The recipe as it stands is no for me. I am keeping the best of the best for my family tastes and this didn't cut it.
The BEST deviled eggs I have ever made or eaten! Delicious! This is the only recipe I use now for lil devils.
This recipe is so delicious I made with regular yellow mustard and Dijon mustard and it was amazing! Even my husband like it and said to me always make it the same. THANKS!
I had the mustards called for on hand so gave this a go. Solid eggs with an extra 1-2tablespoons mayo to suit my taste.
This is my go-to devilled egg recipe. I love the sweet, hot and spicy mixture.
